posts.cooked:
Do the Sentinels each count for a hero toward the "H" count, or do they collectively still count as one? It wouldn't make sense to scale the villians that much despite having four playable hero character cards, but I just wanted to clarify.

Thanks!

posts.name: Ameena
posts.cooked: They do count as four hero targets, though. If something hits all hero targets, they all get hit. If something hits all heroes, only one of them will (your choice). If they didn't count as a single hero then stuff like Plague Rat's flip mechanic would be messed up (because he'd never be able to Infect everyone).
posts.raw: They do count as four hero [i]targets[/i], though. If something hits all hero targets, they all get hit. If something hits all [i]heroes[/i], only one of them will (your choice). If they didn't count as a single hero then stuff like Plague Rat's flip mechanic would be messed up (because he'd never be able to Infect everyone).

posts.name: Killswitch
posts.cooked:
Whenever a card affects a hero's hand or trash, the card refers to "a hero." Since The Sentinels isn't the first deck to deal with multiple targets (Unity's droids, Expatriette's flak jacket, Visionary's projection), I believe there has been no problem with affecting an entire hero's board as far as taking damage. It's always been referred to as hero targets.

So yeah, I fully understand what a hero TARGET is. I just wasn't sure if each Sentinel in that deck counts toward "H," since they can each be incapacitated, each have a power, etc.
